name: Villa Empain (Boghossian Foundation)
funding: Run by the Boghossian Foundation, created in 1992 by the jewellers Robert Boghossian and his sons, which bought and restored the villa. The Circle of the Villa adds donors.

name: Angkor Panorama Museum
funding: Mansudae built it with North Korean money, reported at US$24 million, and co-ran it with Cambodia's APSARA Authority. Its director said in 2016 Mansudae would take ten years' profit.

name: Arthur Erickson House and Garden
funding: Owned by the Arthur Erickson Foundation, a charity that takes donations and tour fees. Canadian Heritage gave CAD 17,800 in 2024. Patrons include Michael Audain and Yosef Wosk.

name: Jurkovič Villa
funding: Branch of the Moravian Gallery, founded by the Ministry of Culture, which paid CZK 140.9M of its CZK 168.0M 2025 income. A Norwegian Financial Mechanism grant supported the villa.

name: Villa Stiassni
funding: The National Heritage Institute runs it. Transfers, mostly from the Ministry of Culture, were 69 percent of 2024 revenue. EU's ERDF paid 85 percent of a CZK 179M restoration project.

name: Villa Tugendhat
funding: Brno City Museum, funded by the City of Brno: CZK 108.3M of CZK 199.2M income in 2025. State budget and funds CZK 4.6M, South Moravian Region CZK 0.35M.

name: Bauer Villa
funding: Ministry of Culture paid CZK 38.4M in 2025 for the villa and furniture; the Museum of Decorative Arts runs it. An EEA grant covered EUR 348k of the earlier restoration.

name: Brummel House (Adolf Loos in Pilsen)
funding: The Brummel family owns the house. Plzeň - TURISMUS, a City of Pilsen organisation, runs the tours. The Adolf Loos Plzeň project credits Ministry for Regional Development state-budget money.

name: Semler Residence
funding: Plzeň Region owns the building and gave the Gallery of West Bohemia CZK 37M of its CZK 39M 2024 budget. Region and EU funds helped pay the EUR 4.5M restoration.

name: Villa Bílek
funding: Run by the Prague City Gallery, which the City of Prague founded and pays: CZK 122.8M operating contribution in 2024, against CZK 10.8M own revenue. Four patrons gave CZK 360,000.

name: Villa Müller
funding: Owned by the City of Prague and run by the Museum of Prague, a city organisation that received a CZK 227.9M city subsidy in 2024.

name: Villa Rothmayer
funding: Run by the Museum of Prague, which the City of Prague funds with a CZK 227.9M subsidy (2024). The museum site also names the Education Ministry and Erasmus as supporters.
